Inscribed on the edge of the frame with the seal "Collection under the supervision of Lord Xin".　　It is one of the characteristics of Song dynasty miniatures that they are good at capturing the momentary scenes to express the vitality of nature. This painting depicts two small birds playing and fighting on a flat slope, rolling together in a ball. The artist uses a combination of real and imaginary, highlighting the focus of the painting method, the wings and tail plumes of the birds are only roughly written dynamic, the head and abdominal feathers are lightly dyed and lightly drawn. What is portrayed is the claws and beaks of the finches and the eyes of the two finches looking at each other. In the picture, the bird with the upper hand holds the other's beak in its left paw, while the right paw holds the other's claw and is about to peck, but its beak is also held by the other, forming a stalemate in which no one can peck, which is quite interesting. The wings of both birds are wide open, and the sense of motion and strength is fully reflected here. It is difficult to imagine this scene, but it is the result of careful observation.　　There is an inscription by Geng Zhaozhong on the opposite side of the painting: "Huang Juyuan was able to carry on his family's learning, and his dots and dyes have a simple and wild look. The history of painting is judged by Huang's richness, which may not be without criticism. Thousand Hills Geng Xin Gong."
